learning_outcomes.text: Be original in the development and application of ideas, within a research environment.
Solution of problem in new and unfamiliar multidisciplinary environments, related to its knowledge area.
Integration of knowledge, facing the complexity of issuing judgments and sentences parting from some information that includes ethic and social liability constraints.
Ability of communicating justified decisions and conclusions, to specialized and unspecialized listeners.
Ability of autonomous learning.
Critical analysis of the information coming from the sensing and instrumentation subsystems.
Practical and experimental verification of monitoring and controlling electrical energy conversion systems, including safety operation of electric systems
Skills related to teamwork, recognizing different roles within a group and different ways of organizing research teams.
Ability to manage information: search, analysis and synthesis of the specific technical information.
Ability to assimilate and communicate information in English concerning technical documents.
Ability to plan and organize work
Skills for critical reasoning, making decisions and making judgments based on information that include reflecting on social and ethical responsibilities of professional activity
Concern for quality and achievement motivation
Understanding of the importance and the area of utilization of electrical power systems for generation, transmission and distribution of electrical energy
Characterization and modelling of the main energy sources and electric power loads
Ability to understand the basics of the dynamic modelling of electrical power systems.
Characterization, operation and design of electronic topologies and control methods for electric energy conversion
Selection of the digital system best suited for the characteristics of power system control.
To use and program the various peripherals in a digital system for use in power system control.
Designing control programs according to a pattern that allows the reuse of code.
Understanding the limitations of the designed solution and be able to propose alternatives to analyze the increase in cost.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Microcontrollers: Applications, characteristics, manufacturers, features, etc.
Programming environments and debugging tools for microcontrollers.
Organization of the internal memory of a microcontroller
Peripherals (A / D converter, Specific control modules, PWM, input capture, etc.).

assessment_methods.method: Written tests (objective tests, short answer tests and / or test development)
Oral tests (individual, group, presentation of topics/projects, etc.)

assessment_rules: The final student's qualification is obtained as follows: 40% from works/projects (30%) and simulated task performance tests (10%), with a minimum of 40% required for this system. 20% comes from oral tests on topics developed in projects/simulations. Another 30% comes from two individual written tests (one for basic programming and one for specific microcontroller programming), with a minimum of 40% required for this system. The remaining 10% comes from attendance to presential hours, with a minimum of 80% attendance required. For part-time students, a differentiated assessment procedure applies: the "Observation techniques" mark is not included, and the total grade is calculated proportionally to the remaining percentages. Oral tests for part-time students will be scheduled on an agreed date, and online oral presentations are available; other tests might be moved if non-attendance is justified.
